problem: Large VLA navigation policies must run off-board and suffer inference plus WiFi latency (up to seconds), so actions are computed from stale observations and the robot collides with static obstacles and pedestrians. Existing fast-slow VLAs target manipulation with small (~300 ms) delays and predictable dynamics.
motivation: Mobile robots have limited FOV and must react to dynamic obstacles using the freshest observation, yet cannot carry big GPUs. Inspired by cascaded control (slow outer loop, fast inner loop), a small onboard policy can compensate for the delay of the big remote VLA while inheriting its semantic guidance.
key_idea: Run a large OmniVLA remotely and a 76M-parameter onboard Edge Adapter that takes the VLA's delayed action-token embeddings plus the current and delayed low-res images, trained end-to-end with reactive-trajectory up-weighting, to output fresh actions.
insight: The onboard adapter can correct stale guidance because it sees the current image and the (I_t, I_{t-k}) pair, and is trained on samples where the action changes strongly within a chunk. Removing end-to-end finetuning (frozen VLA) drops pose-conditioned SR from 0.85 to 0.25, showing that aligning VLA and adapter is crucial. Under artificial 0.2-5 s workstation latency, the gap to OmniVLA grows with latency (breakdown: AsyncVLA at 0.2 Hz still gets 0.80 SR static / 0.50 with pedestrians vs OmniVLA 0.00).
method: Base VLA: OmniVLA (8.26B; SigLIP+DINOv2+LLaMA2-7B) on workstation processes delayed image I_{t-k} and goal (2D pose/language); its 8x4x4096 action-token embeddings are compressed by a token projector (two MLP ResNet blocks) to 8x1024 tokens.

Edge Adapter: 76M small ViT on Jetson Orin; inputs are the 8 projected action tokens plus a token from EfficientNet-B0 features of the current 96x96 image and one from a 6-channel concatenation of I_t and I_{t-k}; only the output token for I_t goes to a 4-layer MLP action head predicting an N=8 chunk of 2D poses at 3 Hz.

Reactive trajectory up-weighting: compare reference chunks A^t and A^{t-k}; samples whose final-pose distance exceeds d_th=1.0 m are up-weighted (half of each batch), plus prioritizing SACSoN pedestrian samples.

Two-stage end-to-end training: first train adapter and projector with VLA frozen, then finetune all (LoRA ~5% params on the VLA) with imitation loss on absolute and relative poses plus smoothness loss.

Asynchronous system: robot streams timestamped images via WiFi/ROS, buffers them, matches returned embedding timestamps to retrieve I_{t-k}, runs the adapter at ~8 Hz, and a PD controller tracks the waypoints (velocity commands at 10 Hz).

setting.backbone: OmniVLA (LLaMA2-7B, SigLIP+DINOv2; LoRA finetuned) + Edge Adapter (small ViT, EfficientNet-B0, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: GNM datasets (RECON, CoryHall, TartanDrive, Seattle, SCAND, GO Stanford 4), LeLaN in-the-wild language data, SACSoN/HuRoN pedestrian data; uniformly sampled across the three
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (fisheye), 96x96 for adapter, plus external tracking camera for robot pose/goal
setting.action_space: chunk of 8 predicted 2D waypoints (3 Hz, 2.4 s horizon) tracked by a PD controller producing linear/angular velocity
setting.privileged: External tracking camera for robot/goal pose in pose-conditioned navigation

results: AsyncVLA reaches 85% collision-free success on pose-conditioned navigation vs 45% for OmniVLA (strongest baseline), 25% for OmniVLA-edge and 25% for the no-E2E variant, and is also fastest (59.18 s). On OOD language following it gets 0.75 vs 0.83 for OmniVLA and 0.50 for OmniVLA-edge, so it largely preserves VLA semantics.
limitations: Requires an open-weight base VLA that can be finetuned end-to-end, which the authors found crucial.
Limited dynamic-interaction data in navigation datasets; evaluation is small-scale and real-world only, on one low-speed robot (0.3 m/s) with an external tracking camera for pose.
Performance still degrades at very low VLA rates (0.2 Hz with pedestrians: SR 0.50).
compares_to: Leave the Feature Extraction to the Foundation Model (Sendai et al., frozen-VLA adapter)
